1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night
It had been raining for three days straight in Doldari. Kim Haneul’s older sister had gone to Seoul in the spring, and since then, Haneul had been running the village’s small apothecary alone.
When night fell, she secured the outer door, counted the day’s earnings, snuffed the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
Just after she lay down, someone knocked frantically on the door downstairs, and a man’s voice called out, “Is anyone here?”

A young man stood outside the door, soaked through. Blood had seeped into the cloth wrapped around his left arm. The man introduced himself as Park Junho and said he was from the Azure Dragon Society.
“Please treat my wound,” Park Junho said in a low voice. “I’ll pay. Would three thousand five hundred won be enough?”
He pulled a letter wrapped in oiled paper from inside his coat. “This letter must be delivered to Cheongpungsa by the eighteenth of May.”
Haneul thought to herself. The neighbors had been so jealous of how well the apothecary was doing that their stomachs ached, and now a stranger had turned up in the middle of the night.
Even so, Haneul did not take his money. All she said was, “I’ll take you up the mountain first thing tomorrow morning.”
2: As soon as day dawned, the two of them set out. Haneul had a basket strapped to her back, containing rice balls, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain, they met Lee Youngsoo, an old man chopping firewood. The old man set down his axe and spoke in a low voice. The previous evening, three strangers had been searching the edge of the village for a young man who had been injured.
“Haneul, take the cross path,” Lee Youngsoo said. “The main road is dangerous.” Haneul thanked the old man.
The cross path was narrow and slippery. Haneul took the lead, planting her feet firmly one step at a time. Park Junho followed behind in silence.
By noon, the rain had stopped and the mountain mist was slowly lifting, revealing the distant roof of Cheongpungsa. Sister Jeonghye, the nun who welcomed visitors to the temple, stood at the gate.
Jeonghye took the letter, checked the red seal on it, and nodded. “The abbot has been waiting 2 years for this letter.”
Park Junho said to Haneul, “I owe you my life.” Haneul smiled and replied, “Then when you next visit, please fix the apothecary’s roof for me.” Park remained at the temple.
Toward evening, Haneul came down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home, it was already dark. She lit the lamp and sat for a long while behind the counter.
